summary: Describes the process for registering new BGP path attribute type codes with IANA. It points to the basic attribute types described in the BGP specification of the time.

eli5.summary: If you want to add a new field to BGP, you need to get a unique ID for it. This explains how to ask.

questions: how to register a bgp attribute type
subtitle: How to register new attribute types for the Border Gateway Protocol.

tldr.problem: As BGP evolved, new path attributes were needed to carry additional routing information, but there was no formal process for assigning unique type codes.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC establishes that new BGP attribute types must be documented in an RFC, then registered with IANA. During development, implementers use a reserved code (255); once assigned, they update their code and documentation.
tldr.outcome: Provides a framework for extending BGP with new attributes while maintaining interoperability through centralized IANA registration.

today: RFC 2042 remains the reference for BGP attribute type registration. The process has been used successfully for decades to extend BGP with new capabilities.

sections.title: BGP Attribute Types
sections.content:
BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) uses path attributes to carry routing information along with network prefixes. Each attribute has a numeric type code that identifies what kind of information it contains, such as the origin of a route, the path of autonomous systems it traversed, or the next hop.

As BGP deployments evolved, new attributes were needed for features like route reflection and BGP communities, requiring a formal process for assigning new type codes.
sections.eli5: BGP uses numbered tags to label different kinds of routing information attached to routes. This RFC explains how to create new tags.

sections.title: Registration Process
sections.content:
All new BGP attribute types must be documented in an RFC. During development, implementers use the reserved octet value 255 as a placeholder. Once development is complete, the attributes are submitted for registration with IANA (Internet Assigned Numbers Authority).

IANA assigns an official type code number, after which the RFC and the implementation are updated to use the assigned code. Requests should be sent to IANA@IANA.ORG with the subject line including BGP Attribute Type. IANA publishes all assigned values in the periodically updated Assigned Numbers RFC.
sections.eli5: To create a new BGP tag, document it in an RFC, then ask IANA for an official number. During testing, you can use 255 as a temporary number.

sections.title: Currently Defined Attributes
sections.content:
At the time of this RFC, thirteen attribute types were in use: ORIGIN (the source of the route), AS_PATH (the autonomous systems traversed), NEXT_HOP (where to send the packet), MULTI_EXIT_DISC (exit preference), LOCAL_PREF (local preference), ATOMIC_AGGREGATE, AGGREGATOR (route aggregation info), COMMUNITY (grouping routes), ORIGINATOR_ID, CLUSTER_LIST (for route reflection), DPA, ADVERTISER, and RCID_PATH.

All defined attribute types and their codes are maintained in the IANA registry and the Assigned Numbers RFC.
sections.eli5: BGP uses many standard tags for different kinds of routing information, from which network sent the route to which path it should take.
